text:
gpu-monitor-bot: alert — rising correctable ECC + page retirements detected on gpu-node-usw2-42 (GPU 1 / UUID GPU-9a8b7c). 5xx -> 47 correctable events in last 6h, 3 page retirements. tagging @infra-oncall.

sanjay: seeing the same in our telemetry. memory-correctable-rate spiked at 03:12 UTC, node has steady load but not overheating (68C).

amanda: can someone paste the nvml/nvidia-smi memory section? want to confirm retire count and remap events.

ben: pasted from the node a minute ago:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
GPU 0000:3B:00.0
    FB Memory Usage
        Total                       : 32768 MiB
        Used                        : 9124 MiB
        Free                        : 23644 MiB
    ECC Errors
        Volatile
            Single-bit ECC errors    : 47
            Double-bit ECC errors    : 0
    Page Retirement
        Retired pages              : 3
        Remapped pages             : 3
```

infra-oncall: ok, that's consistent. Xid errors? any kernel OOMs or process restarts?

eli: kernel logs show these lines around the spikes: `NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:3B:00: Xid (PCI_MASTERSHIP) 31` and `nvidia nvml: page retirement remapping initiated`. No user-visible OOMs.

amanda: we should treat this as degrading GPU. Plan: 1) cordon + drain node 2) migrate pods / jobs 3) mark GPU as replaceable in inventory and open HW ticket 4) track in fleet sheet. agree? :thumbsup:

ben: +1. I'll kick off drain. low-risk window now.

ben: command run: `kubectl drain gpu-node-usw2-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

gpu-monitor-bot: note — live autoscaler will try to reschedule pods to other nodes in the cluster; we've got capacity headroom in the same AZ (us-west-2a) but not much in 2b.

infra-oncall: created issue HW-1452 in internal tracker, assigned to hardware-team, severity P2. details: repeated ECC single-bit increases, 3 page retirements, remap count rising. added node to quarantine label `faulty-gpu`. ticket link: https://redwood.internal/issue/HW-1452

hardware-team: received. will coordinate RMA. can you provide serial + GPU UUID and last 7 days of ECC stats?

ben: serial: SN-7K4Z21, GPU UUID: GPU-9a8b7c. attaching last 7d stats export (uploaded to ticket).

amanda: also adding row to fleet-memory-faults spreadsheet to track trend and replacement timeline: https://go/reports/fleet-memory-faults (row added, note: node, gpu idx, first-detected, page-retirements, current-count, ticket).

eli: a quick note — if we get >10 page retirements in a short window, some kernels will start failing with Xid 79/DMA errors; keep an eye on nodes in same rack. could be card-level wearout.

infra-oncall: action items summarized: 1) ben: finish drain + confirm no pods restarting on this GPU (ETA 20m) 2) hardware-team: RMA + replacement ETA 48-72h 3) ops: update fleet sheet and alert customers if any job impacted 4) gpu-monitor-bot: raise anomaly if remapped_pages > 10 in next 24h.

sanjay: also consider adding this GPU to proactive replacement pool after RMA to avoid swapping new hardware into hot racks. cost vs risk discussion for fleet planning later.

ben: drain complete, all GPU-using pods moved. node cordoned. no evictions failures.

gpu-monitor-bot: follow-up alert at 1753003400 — another single-bit ECC increment observed (now 52 total), remapped pages still 3. monitor threshold not yet hit.

amanda: thanks. leaving quarantine label and we can reprovision once new card is staged. I'll notify customer-facing infra for any potential capacity impacts tomorrow.

hardware-team: acknowledged. will post RMA number once created.

eli: adding note for postmortem: check kernel driver version differences across fleet; we've seen certain NV driver builds mask early remaps. good to correlate.

infra-oncall: closing thread for now, will re-open if remap count increases. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
